kernel_variant: §3.6 cooperative-amax fused decode kernel. Work-group of 64 lanes cooperatively scans X via sub_group_reduce_max; 64x reduction in redundant scan work vs the naive variant.
diagnosis: Cooperative amax via sub_group_reduce_max delivers a real but shape-dependent win. The naive fused kernel had every WI rescan X (1024-way redundancy at decode 4K). The coop kernel reduces that to one scan per work-group (16-way redundancy at 64-lane WG), saving ~134 us at decode 4K hidden.
Net vs B2 + B5 baseline at decode 4K: 410 us vs ~435 us = 6% faster. Smaller than initial estimate but on the right side of zero.

Win is biggest where slice_I is large relative to slice_O (decode 4K, FFN down). When slice_O dominates (FFN up: 11008 / 64 = 173 work-groups, each rescanning X), the matmul work dwarfs the scan and fusion doesn't help.

Confirms the paper §3.7 pattern works — input quantization integrated with the operational kernel via work-group cooperation. The pattern is now in place for future fusion candidates (RMSNorm + residual, RoPE + QKV + layout transform from §3.6 manual fusion).
lessons: fusion is shape-dependent — its value scales with the ratio of pre/post-matmul work to matmul work itself.
sub_group_reduce_max is the right primitive on Adreno (verified cl_khr_subgroups extension available).
reqd_work_group_size(64,1,1) attribute pins the WG = sub-group invariant so sub_group_reduce_max is unambiguous.

future fusion-style improvements should focus on the cases where the fused op contributes meaningful pre/post-matmul cost — RoPE, LayerNorm/RMSNorm, residual add — and on the decode-path matmuls specifically.
